finding_key: packages/cli/test/output.test.ts::`bin entrypoint` tests assert on source text, not behavior; one assertion is vacuous
evidence: Verified against the supplied files. packages/cli/src/bin.ts:13 imports outputError and the comment above the parse call also contains the word, so `expect(source).toContain('outputError')` in the `bin entrypoint` describe (test/output.test.ts, end of file) passes even if the catch body were empty — the assertion is vacuous. The other assertions (`toMatch(/\.catch\(/)`, `toContain('program.parseAsync(')`, `not.toMatch(/program\.parse\s*\(/)`) are pure source-text matches that can be satisfied while the actual rejection-to-envelope behavior is broken (e.g. aliased calls or a removed handler on a different promise), and no test actually drives a rejection through the entrypoint. The claim is accurate; impact is limited to misleading test coverage, since bin.ts itself is currently correct.
